final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key gaps: no evidence of disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, and no final legal determination. The response usefully narrows the claim from clean compliance to a caveated certification theory, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new proof. That distinction matters here: a caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat describes a bounded limitation within a satisfied policy framework. Here, the caveat is itself the unresolved compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows a named customer-committed segment missing target, an open legal review on disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance for material limitations affecting named launch use cases. Aggregate readiness evidence remains relevant to operational support for launch, but it does not close the policy gap. On this record, the certification decision has some evidentiary support on readiness, yet compliance for release without resolved disclosure or risk acceptance remains unresolved; that keeps the result suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the clinical coding assistant limitation was disclosed before launch for a named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance before launch.
The affected segment is named in two hospital revenue-cycle commitments, so materiality remains plausibly triggered under the policy text.
The legal ticket on whether disclosure is required remains open with no final determination.
Aggregate readiness and no Sev-1 rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the internal disclosure predicate for a material limitation.
Public model-card and risk-management guidance support documenting and monitoring limitations, but they do not substitute for the release policy requirement.
